title: Two learners chasing each other
sub: P(heads) for player 1 (across) and player 2 (up), learning simultaneously in matching pennies.

frames.caption: Matching pennies: player 1 wins if the coins match, player 2 if they differ. The only Nash equilibrium is both playing 50/50 (centre). Each player learns with multiplicative weights, raising the probability of whichever action has been paying off. Start slightly off-centre.

Each player chases the other's last move: as player 1 leans heads, tails becomes better for player 2, which makes tails better for player 1, and so on. The strategies cycle around the equilibrium instead of settling: each learner's environment is the other learner, and it keeps moving.

Worse, the cycles widen: the actual strategies spiral out towards the corners. Yet the time-averaged strategies (green) converge to the 50/50 equilibrium. This is a general fact for zero-sum games: no-regret learners converge on average, not in their actual play.
